summary.text: Mary Keefe is a Democratic state representative from the 15th Worcester District who has served in the Massachusetts House of Representatives since 2013 and is seeking re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election.
Before her election she spent twelve years as executive director of the Pleasant Street Neighborhood Network Center in Worcester.

paragraphs.text: Mary Keefe is originally from Sutton and has lived in downtown Worcester for more than thirty years.
Her biography lists a bachelor of fine arts from Massachusetts College of Art, and she has worked as an art educator at the Worcester Art Museum.
She was executive director of the Pleasant Street Neighborhood Network Center, a resident-led organization in Worcester's Piedmont area, for twelve years before she was elected.
Keefe took office on January 2, 2013, succeeding Vincent Pedone.

Her official biography says she worked on the underlying legislation for the 2018 criminal justice reform act, was a lead sponsor of the Student Opportunity Act signed in November 2019, and co-chairs the Legislative Criminal Justice Reform Caucus.

She is vice chair of the Joint Committee on Consumer Protection and Professional Licensure and also serves on the Joint Committees on Mental Health, Substance Use and Recovery, on Racial Equity, Civil Rights, and Inclusion, and on Tourism, Arts and Cultural Development.

Keefe's biography lists her as a founding member of Progressive Democrats of Massachusetts and the Worcester Community Labor Coalition, a co-chair of Worcester Interfaith, and a board member of the Green Hill Park Coalition.
